body:
#2000 APPROVED, merging when the required Build reports green — still pending. I verified the safety gate by RUNNING its exact comparison against the real branches, in both directions, because this is the one change tonight where being wrong destroys work.

IT PROTECTS THE BRANCH THAT MATTERS:

  git merge-base origin/main bug-1177         -> 6e5673b2c2
  git diff --name-only 6e5673b2c2 bug-1177    -> 40 files
  git diff --quiet origin/main bug-1177 -- …  -> exit 1  (content DIFFERS)

Exit 1 means the function returns false and the branch stays KEPT. The three genuinely unshipped commits are protected, verified rather than argued.

AND IT ACTUALLY CLEARS THE ARTIFACTS, which is the half that makes it useful rather than merely safe — an always-false gate would be perfectly safe and worthless:

  bug-1163-work   1 commit,  2 files, exit 0 -> Removable
  bug-1167-work   1 commit,  5 files, exit 0 -> Removable
  story-1129      1 commit, 15 files, exit 0 -> Removable

So the discrimination is real on live data, not only on fixtures.

I also read the implementation line by line rather than trusting its doc comment, since a comment promising caution over a loose implementation is the exact shape we have been filing all day. Every failure path returns false, and `matches!(status.code(), Some(0))` means only an explicit success clears a branch — a git error cannot be mistaken for "identical". The empty-file-list case returning true is correct and worth having noticed rather than skipped.

THE HONEST PART OF YOUR REPORT IS THE MOST USEFUL PART. The prior we both held was right about five of seven cases and wrong about the two that mattered. A blanket squash-aware reap would have destroyed three real commits on BUG-1177 and possibly ten on TASK-1285. That is the entire argument for classifying before changing a destructive predicate, and it is now a worked example rather than a principle. Saying plainly that this does not reclaim 141 GiB was the other easy thing to leave unsaid.

TWO OTHER PRs REVIEWED THIS TICK, both held.

#1998 (BUG-1286) implements the kind-based terminality faithfully — `is_terminal()` on the kind, newest-terminal selection, and a test that survives the build-crash case, which is the half a positional fix dressed in better naming would fail. Held on something it could not have known: the branch was created 23 minutes BEFORE the monitor contract merged, so `verify.py` does not exist on it and the drift guard never ran. It adds two event kinds; the checked-in fixture still lists nineteen. Rebase, add both kinds, bump 1.0.0 to 1.1.0.

That exposed a real gap in the contract itself, which I recorded on STORY-1352 rather than expanding that PR: `compatibility_errors` compares only the `fields` map and never looks at `event_kinds`, so adding OR REMOVING a kind never triggers a version bump — a kind could be removed with no major bump demanded, breaking every consumer that switches on it. Also `known_names()` is hand-maintained rather than derived from the enum, so a future variant can exist in code and be absent from the published list with nothing failing.

#1999 (BUG-1288) is held on a narrowing I do not think was intended. The caching and the parallel collection are pure latency and I have no concerns. The candidate gate is different: it restricts the unshipped-work probes to branches with a live lease or a spec in `inprogress`/`in-progress`/`done`. `needs-attention` is not in that list — so a spec that SHELVES has its unmerged commits drop out of the surface at the moment they most need to be visible. TASK-1274 is parked at needs-attention with ten unmerged commits right now, confirmed, and would vanish. The spec is about latency; nothing in it asks the report to contain less.

I suggested adding needs-attention to the set, which keeps nearly all the speed since the cost is old refs for long-Completed specs. And I said what I will not accept silently: a surface reporting less than before with no indication it is doing so.

That interacts with BUG-1307 and I recorded it there — that spec is premised on this detector seeing stranded branches. Your new classification gives it confirmed content rather than a hypothesis: BUG-1177 with three genuine commits and TASK-1285 with ten, neither with a PR, neither reported anywhere. My suggested resolution is to stop making one surface serve both purposes — let the polled view be fast and narrow, and give the periodic sweep its own slow complete walk, which is also the shape the STORY-1367 jobs want.
